title: Preservation before constructible restriction
statement:
Use $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and the categories $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], with the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; put $c=2e$.

Then, for every $K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions have a common
cohomological interval $[a,b]$, one has
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y_{\Proet},A),&
  Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A),\\
  Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(X'_{\Proet},A),&
  Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A).
 \end{aligned}
$$
The reductions of $Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ have cohomology supported in $[a,b]$. The reductions of $Rf_*K$, $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K$, and $Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ have cohomology supported in $[a,b+c]$. Here a reduction amplitude bound means containment of cohomological support, not equality or a Tor-amplitude assertion.

*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this preservation: the
constructibility of the four outputs is the adic constructibility of
Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag 09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1))
and Proposition 61.29.7 ([Tag
09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)), and the amplitude bounds
are those of Lemma 59.92.2 ([Tag
095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) and Theorem 63.14.5 ([Tag
0GL0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GL0)), each stated for a single
complex on a Noetherian scheme; the closest packaged form is Lemma 61.29.2
([Tag 09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)), which realizes one
constructible $K$ as $\Rlim K_n$ with a common interval and etale origins
but says nothing about functors. The blueprint adds the simultaneous
statement for the completed pullbacks and direct images of
$\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions share the interval $[a,b]$.

proof.text: The residue field $A/I$ has characteristic $\ell$, so $\ell\mid N$. Write $N=\ell d$; the element $dN^{-1}$ is an inverse of $\ell$ on all four schemes. Thus the scheme hypotheses in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] hold. The given properness, noetherianity, finite dimension and geometric fibre bound meet every hypothesis of [thm-weil-pbc-amplification-proper], giving $\mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e)$. In [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification] this supplies FIN for both proper maps at every level and interval-preserving finite pullbacks. The input $K$ is complete and its canonical reduction tower has the local models of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. On those strata and covers, its reduction cohomology is finite lisse by the displayed local reduction isomorphisms in that definition, hence intrinsically constructible. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], each $K_n$ is in the finite-coefficient bounded constructible category, in the assumed interval $[a,b]$. Throughout, this equivalence uses the global finite-stratification constructibility convention stated in that node; the schemes are Noetherian.

source.place: Proof, canonical-reduction refinement of the four-output argument

proof.text: For each output it suffices to check completeness and intrinsically constructible canonical reductions in one common interval. Indeed, for a complete $J$ with such reductions $J_n$ on one of the four schemes $T$, [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] supplies the canonical strict tower and its normalization isomorphisms, inducing its transitions and satisfying the quotient cocycle. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-constructible-local-effectivity]: its Noetherian and uniform-interval hypotheses hold, so this very tower admits the common local models and normalization-compatible isomorphisms required by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. Choose bounded constructible origins at every level by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-etale-origin-witnesses] to these origins and the canonical normalizations to obtain compatible witnesses. These data and the assumed completeness are precisely membership in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. This is an assembly of the cited statements on the canonical tower; it does not identify any independently supplied TOW quotient structures.

source.place: Proof, canonical-reduction refinement of the four-output argument

proof.text: We will transfer finite constructibility using cohomology only. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], the constant sheaves $\underline{P_n}$ are the coefficient sheaves $(P_n)_T$ of the adic datum and $\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}=A_T$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] gives $A_T/I^nA_T\cong(P_n)_T$, i.e. $\pi_n:A_T\to(P_n)_T$ is a surjection of sheaves with kernel $I^nA_T$. An $A_T$-linear map $\phi$ between $(P_n)_T$-modules, regarded as $A_T$-modules by restriction along $\pi_n$, is therefore $(P_n)_T$-linear: locally lift a section $r$ of the quotient to $\widetilde r$ of $A_T$ and compute $\phi(rx)=\phi(\widetilde r x)=\widetilde r\phi(x)=r\phi(x)$. A different lift changes both expressions by zero; the equalities glue. Thus an isomorphism of underlying completed-coefficient complexes gives quotient-linear isomorphisms of their genuine quotient-module cohomology sheaves. This argument asserts no lifting of the isomorphism to a quotient-coefficient derived category.

source.place: Proof, canonical-reduction refinement of the four-output argument

proof.text: Put $H=Rf_*K$. Its completeness follows from [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. The projection formula [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], applied with the perfect finite quotient $P_n$, identifies the underlying completed-coefficient complexes of the actual $H_n$ and the finite direct image $Rf_*K_n$. By step 3 their cohomology isomorphisms are quotient-linear. FIN for $f$ from step 1 and [prop-weil-pbc-restriction-direct-image] put the finite direct images in the bounded constructible category in $[a,b+2e]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], this gives intrinsically constructible cohomology and the same bound on the actual $H_n$. Step 2, on their canonical normalization maps, gives $H\in\Dbc(Y_{\Proet},A)$ and the stated interval. No comparison of supplied quotient normalizations is needed.

source.place: Proof, canonical-reduction refinement of the four-output argument

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] to $(g',K)$ and $(g,H)$, both with complete input. It gives complete outputs $B=Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ and $C=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}H$, with isomorphisms $B_n\cong Lg_n'^*K_n$ and $C_n\cong Lg_n^*H_n$ in the actual quotient-coefficient derived categories. Step 4 gave the intrinsic constructibility and interval of $H_n$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] makes these finite bounded constructible inputs, as already known for $K_n$. Apply the interval-preserving pullback clauses of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification], supplied by step 1. The intervals are $[a,b]$ for $B_n$ and $[a,b+2e]$ for $C_n$. The derived-origin equivalence gives intrinsic constructibility of their cohomology. Step 2 on each canonical tower proves $B\in\Dbc(X'_{\Proet},A)$ and $C\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A)$, with these intervals.

source.place: Proof, canonical-reduction refinement of the four-output argument

proof.text: Finally put $D=Rf'_*B$. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] it is complete. The projection formula [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] compares the underlying completed-coefficient complexes of $D_n$ and the finite direct image $Rf'_*B_n$; step 3 makes their cohomology isomorphisms quotient-linear. Step 5 gives finite bounded constructible $B_n$ in $[a,b]$. FIN for $f'$ with the same $c=2e$ from step 1 and [prop-weil-pbc-restriction-direct-image] give $Rf'_*B_n$ finite bounded constructible in $[a,b+2e]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] and the cohomology isomorphisms, the actual $D_n$ are intrinsically constructible with this bound. Step 2 yields $D\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A)$. The four outputs and their four bounds are those asserted, with the pullback of $H$ retaining $H$'s interval $[a,b+2e]$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with
$X,Y,X',Y'$ noetherian of finite dimension, $f$ and $f'$ proper, and suppose
there is a positive integer $N$ annihilating $A/I$ which is invertible on
all four schemes. Assume that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at
most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; put $c=2e$.

Then, for every $K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ whose reductions have a common
cohomological interval $[a,b]$, one has
$$
 \begin{aligned}
  Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y_{\Proet},A),&
  Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A),\\
  Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(X'_{\Proet},A),&
  Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K&\in\Dbc(Y'_{\Proet},A).
 \end{aligned}
$$
The two pullbacks have reduction amplitude $[a,b]$ and the two direct images
have reduction amplitude contained in $[a,b+c]$.

proof.text:
By [thm-weil-pbc-amplification-proper] the three conditions
$$
 \mathrm{AMP}(\square;2e),\qquad\mathrm{WIT}(\square),\qquad\mathrm{TOW}(\square)
$$
of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification],
[def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] and [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation]
hold for $c=2e$, so the argument below applies. Let
$K\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$ have all reductions supported in $[a,b]$, so that
its reduction tower is uniformly bounded constructible in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] with compatible etale-origin
witnesses. By the amplification $\mathrm{AMP}(\square;c)$ and the tower
preservation $\mathrm{TOW}(\square)$, the levelwise tower functors carry
this tower to uniformly bounded constructible towers whose local models have
amplitude compatible with the containments, and by the witness compatibility
of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] the compatible etale-origin
witnesses are carried to compatible witnesses. By the reconstruction lemma
for uniform towers each of the four derived limits is then realized by its
local models, hence lies in the bounded constructible complete category, is
derived complete and has the stated reduction amplitude; and by the
direct-image-limits proposition the four limits are exactly $Rf_*K$,
$Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K$, $Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ and
$Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$, which proves the assertions.
